channel.title: Our Favourite Places Yorkshire Events
channel.description: Upcoming Yorkshire events from Our Favourite Places.

item.title: Wall Hanging Workshop with Sanpo x The Joint
item.description: Join illustrative artist Sanpo at new art shop The Joint. You’ll be given all the tools and guidance you need to create your own original linen wall hanging, ready to gift or hang at home.
item.location: The Joint, Unit 7, Chaucer Yard, Clough Road, Highfield, S1 4TE
item.ify:location: The Joint, Unit 7, Chaucer Yard, Clough Road, Highfield, S1 4TE
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Zawose Queens
item.description: Pendo and Leah Zawose, two women from a famous Tanzanian musical family, take their place as lead vocalists and performers. Their music is rooted in traditional singing and instrumentation, with contemporary touches of leftfield pop and synth-funk.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Nish Kumar: Angry Humour From A Really Nice Guy
item.description: Kumar is 40. His mind is breaking. His body is worse. Expect existential angst and political disquiet from comedy’s cheekiest boy.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Chopin Nocturnes
item.description: "Poet of the piano” Pavel Kolesnikov is one of the world’s most exciting young pianists. Lauded for his amazing ability to cast new light on familiar repertoire, he makes his Music in the Round debut with a tour through Chopin's complete Nocturnes.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: SPO play Mahler, Farrenc and Bottesini
item.description: Sheffield Philharmonic Orchestra play Mahler’s Symphony no.5, Farrenc overture no.2 and Bottesini concerto for double bass.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Endless Love Creative: Winter Makers Market
item.description: Discover artisan craft, contemporary design and beautifully made work from 65 independent makers, set across two floors in the heart of Sheffield.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Bookbinding Workshop: Junk Journal
item.description: Create your own junk journal with Concrete Nature as part of Endless Love Creative Market.
item.location: Showroom Work Station, 15 Paternoster Row, S1 2BX
item.ify:location: Showroom Work Station, 15 Paternoster Row, S1 2BX
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Day of Dance
item.description: Come and celebrate the joy of dance as part of the Dancing Sheffield project. Including a mass join-in dance in Weston Park, performances, workshops and more.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Sylvie + Ursula
item.description: The duo of rising London-based vocalist Sylvie Noble and BBC Young Jazz Musician of the Year 2025 Ursula Harrison (double bass) bring their beautifully poised, playful, resonant and captivating music to Jazz at The Lescar.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: WTF: Pink Floyd - The Wall
item.description: A confined but troubled rock star descends into madness as he physically and socially isolates himself from everyone. Screening as part of WTF, Showroom's monthly screening strand celebrating the films that make you say "What The F...ilm"!?
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Kelham Makes: Festive Wreath Making
item.description: Get crafty this Christmas and learn how to create a festive fresh door wreath to take home.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
item.description: When his wife dies, a religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith and fatherhood sets out on a desperate journey to protect his children. A gripping, inventive tale on religion and morality with a standout performance from Mahershala Ali.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Cabaret Schmabaret
item.description: An evening of fun, filth and frivolity with comedy, games and the debut of a new play UBU Royale. Presented by the Performers’ Playground. Advisory age 14+.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Bellot Ensemble
item.description: The award-winning vibrant, period instrument group present Heroines of the Seicento.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: You Can See Everything
item.description: Notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a film crew to document her 34 days before she’s sent to prison. What begins as an intimate portrait becomes a mind-bending unraveling of certainty. One of 2026's most unforgettable films.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: FFStival: Sheffield’s Female-led Film Festival
item.description: FFStival returns for year three!
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Gods Are Not to Blame
item.description: Join Utopia Theatre for an afternoon of African theatre, music, culture and community. Culminating in an exclusive theatrical presentation of Ola Rotimi's celebrated play The Gods Are Not to Blame.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Third Bite Dance: PCK Residency with 50+CDS
item.description: PCK are developing a new work for Third Bite Dance (the University resident group of older performers) in a four-day workshop this autumn.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Candlelit Mozart Requiem
item.description: Come and hear the Cathedral Choir with West Riding Ensemble perform Mozart's Requiem, Coronation Mass, and Ave verum corpus in a candlelit setting.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Quirkus Circus: Anti-Christmas Cabaret
item.description: Expect the unexpected in the surreal, joyous, raucous world of Quirkus Circus. Hosting the night is Velma Von Bon Bon, with a cocktail of glamour, comedy, puppetry and circus skills.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Yorkshire Artspace Open Studios
item.description: Each November, over a hundred creative residents at Yorkshire Artspace's two sites open their doors to the public for one weekend. Meet some of Sheffield's talented artists, nosy around their creative workplaces, and enjoy exhibitions of their work.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: False Autumn
item.description: An exhibition by James Clarkson, tracing the ways that work-related pressures can enter the rhythms of everyday life.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: John Shuttleworth: It's Nice Up North [+Q&A]
item.description: A special, 20th-anniversary screening tour of Graham Fellows’ much loved comedy documentary It’s Nice Up North. Also presented as a tribute to the late Martin Parr, who shot the film.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: All of a Sudden
item.description: Marie-Lou runs a nursing home outside Paris. She meets Mari, a Japanese playwright who is terminally ill. From Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (director of the phenomenal Drive My Car), this transformative film explores connection and a radical idea of care.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Grass
item.description: Screening of the silent masterpiece Grass (1925) with live music by Peyman Yazdanian and Adib Rostami.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Doctor Who: The Satan Pit
item.description: Celebrate Doctor Who Day with an exclusive big-screen event marking 20 years of the Tenth Doctor and Rose Tyler.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Health by Numbers: Demystifying Digital Health Data
item.description: An interactive exhibition exploring how smartphone and wearable devices create and understand our health information.
item.location: Langsett Expo Hall, Langsett Building, S1 2LX (entrance off Howard St)
item.ify:location: Langsett Expo Hall, Langsett Building, S1 2LX (entrance off Howard St)
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Online Talk: Jyll Bradley In Conversation with Ben Harman
item.description: In this insightful and thought-provoking conversation, British artist Jyll Bradley will join Ben Harman, Senior Curator of Photography at the National Galleries of Scotland, to talk about her extensive body of photographic work.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Maddalena Ghezzi, Ruth Goller, Maria Chiara Argirò
item.description: Jazz at The Lescar present a trio of leading creative musicians from the London scene. With fearless, unique and explorative new music mixing ethereal vocals, atmospheric synths sounds, and visceral bass.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Lambchop
item.description: Brudenell presents: an intimate piano performance from Lambchop. Initially indebted to traditional country, the band’s music has subsequently moved through a range of influences including post-rock, soul and lounge music.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Carmen's Voice
item.description: Carmen was never a love story. This November, Atelier Armonico presents Carmen’s Voice, a new adaptation of Bizet’s iconic opera shaped by women’s lived experiences. Performed in English and featuring a 12-piece chamber orchestra.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Words Are Coming
item.description: Showroom's monthly open mic invites writers of all styles are welcome to perform their work.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Rite of Passage
item.description: A one-man show about what happens when you arrive somewhere new and realise nobody told you the rules. Funny, honest and deeply human.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
item.description: A brilliantly imaginative, dark fantasy stop-motion animated musical. Jack Skellington, the pumpkin king of Halloween Town, discovers Christmas Town and attempts to bring Christmas under his control.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: A Journey Through Nordic Music
item.description: Join a panel of musicians and experts who will shine a light on some of the composers and music featuring across Northern Lights, Music in the Round's weekend of elemental music from the frozen north.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Music from Iceland
item.description: A dazzling portrait of contemporary Icelandic music ranging from celebrated glacial works by Anna Thorvaldsdóttir and Oscar-winning Hildur Guðnadóttir, to new arrangements of Björk and Ólafur Arnalds’ haunting music for Broadchurch.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Bob Dylan
item.description: Widely acknowledged as one of the most important figures of the modern day and one of the greatest and most influential songwriters of all time, Bob Dylan has reshaped popular music by elevating lyric writing to a profound literary art form.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Pitchblack Playback: My Bloody Valentine - Loveless
item.description: Immerse yourself in My Bloody Valentine's shoegaze-defining classic on a powerful cinema sound system. Pitchblack Playback's listening session in the dark celebrates the album's 35th anniversary.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Sibelius & Grieg
item.description: Music in the Round's resident Ensemble 360 performs masterpieces and miniatures for strings and piano by two giants of Nordic classicism.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Engegård Quartet
item.description: Norway’s multi-award-winning Engegård Quartet brings its customary boldness, energy and freshness to Sheffield in a concert of Mozart, Beethoven and Grieg.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Open Studios and Christmas Market
item.description: Explore inside the historic Portland Works to buy art, ceramics, glass, print, jewellery, textiles and more from the people who make them. With an opportunity to visit studios and share mulled wine and a mince pie with the resident makers.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Adam Hopper & The Wimps
item.description: Sheffield based Adam Hopper and his band play a blend of mellow alternative pop and anti-folk. Drawing inspiration from 70s art-rock, 90s lo-fi and Americana, their sound moves from intimate folk passages to weirder, psych-inspired freak-outs.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: ShAFF Retrospective Features – The Best Of 20 Years
item.description: Sheffield Adventure Film Festival first landed at the Showroom in March 2006. To mark this 20th anniversary, the team have crafted a weekend retrospective of some of the festival's very best features and shorts.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Ukrainian Christmas Market
item.description: Celebrate a Ukrainian Christmas with folk songs, handmade gifts, authentic food and more.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Norwegian Folk
item.description: Formed under the midnight sun in the Lofoten Islands, Norway’s leading string quartet brings the rugged soul of the country to the stage, with arrangements of traditional joiks, haunting psalms and spirited bridal marches.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Christmas 2026
item.description: From family friendly classics to cult festive titles, Showroom's programme will have something for everyone this winter.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: British Jewish Life on Film [+ Q&A]
item.description: An evening of new short films about British Jewish life.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: WTF: Harold and Maude
item.description: Young, rich, and obsessed with death, Harold finds himself changed forever when he meets Maude at a funeral. A 55th anniversary screening.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Snowman + Live Score
item.description: Unite the Union Brass Band present a special festive performance of the Christmas classic with a live score.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Beethoven Appassionata
item.description: Tim Horton performs an afternoon concert for Music in the Round, launching his a journey through Beethoven’s staggering achievements for piano, with works including his celebrated Appassionata sonata.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Reich: Electric Counterpoint
item.description: Scottish guitarist Sean Shibe presents a tour of four centuries of music, including Bach’s first cello suite, Steve Reich’s masterpiece Electric Counterpoint and a recent commission by the UK’s leading contemporary composer Thomas Adès.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Wild Traditions: Arbrevyn
item.description: Arbrevyn perform a Christmas special concert. Featuring Cornish carols alongside more local carols and some of their favourite repertoire.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: New Voices
item.description: Sheffield Chamber Orchestra present a varied introduction to the richness of orchestral music. From Mendelssohn’s enchanted Shakespearean forest to Dvořák’s Czech dances, Handel’s Baroque elegance and Farrenc’s powerful Romantic symphony.
item.location: All Saints Church, Ringinglow Road, S11 7PP
item.ify:location: All Saints Church, Ringinglow Road, S11 7PP
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Lost Christmas [15th Anniversary + Q&A with Suzy Eddie Izzard]
item.description: An urban fairytale from the backstreets of Manchester. Screening followed by an in person Q&A with Suzy Eddie Izzard.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Lacross Club
item.description: Welsh punk band Lacross Club play stupid-on-purpose, gloriously unsubtle, dumb rock-n-roll. Their psychobilly infused garage rock is a vehicle for tales about the pub, beer and hangovers. “My head is poundin’, I spent a hundred pounds in a pub.”
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Great Beyond
item.description: Across four Sundays this December, you can catch classic films from some of the greatest directors of all time.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Kingdom Come - Ten Year Anniversary
item.description: Andro and Eve are having a right royal celebration. Marking ten years of The Kingdom Come drag king cabaret – one of the longest running platforms for drag king talent in the UK!
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Beer and Carols
item.description: Taking you back to Christmas singing assembly. Grab a drink and belt out all your favourite carols with a Cathedral full of people who remember every word (or at least the chorus!).
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Sheffield Beatles Project
item.description: Celebrating their 10th year, the 30-piece Sheffield Beatles Project return for their annual Christmas show, recreating the music of the Fab Four in minute detail. They’ll perform the complete Magical Mystery Tour album, plus favourites and rarities.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
item.description: Charles Dickens’s Christmas Carol can sometimes be a bit of a grizzly tale (especially when the Ghost of Christmas Yet-to-Come appears on the scene), but the Muppets brighten the Christmas tale right up.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Hanging Stars
item.description: Drawing influence from The Byrds, Teenage Fanclub and Big Star, London's Hanging Stars make music full of chiming guitars, four-part harmonies and irresistible melodies. Expect sun-drenched psychedelic folk and beautifully crafted rock songs.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Dune: Part Three [Preview]
item.description: Experience the epic conclusion.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: WTF: The Green Knight
item.description: A loose adaptation of the 14th-century poem Sir Gawain and the Green Knight, notable for its striking imagery and performances. Screening as part of the Showroom's monthly screening strand celebrating films that make you say "What The F...ilm"!?
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Cat Video Fest
item.description: A feature-length theatrical compilation created each year from standout cat videos sourced from public submissions and the wider internet.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Belle and Sebastian
item.description: One of the UK’s most beloved indie pop groups, known for their delicate melodies, captivating storytelling and achingly personal lyrics. This December, they’re celebrating 30 years since the release of their landmark album If You’re Feeling Sinister.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Spotlight: Rocky [50th Anniversary - 4K Restoration]
item.description: Rocky Balboa is a Philadelphia club fighter who seems to be going nowhere. Part of Spotlight, the Showroom's monthly screenings of unforgettable films brought back to the big screen, chosen by staff.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Little Women
item.description: 2019's refreshing adaptation of Louisa May Alcott's beloved novel from writer-director Greta Gerwig, that's both faithful to its beautiful source material and strikingly original. Part of the Showroom's Christmas programme.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Eyes Wide Shut
item.description: Delivered just days before his passing, Stanley Kubrick's mesmerising tale is the ultimate alternative festive film. It returns to the big screen for the Showroom's Christmas 2026 season.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Tokyo Godfathers
item.description: Three homeless people – a former bicycle racer, a trans woman who used to work as a drag queen, and a runaway young girl – live together in Tokyo. On Christmas Eve, they find a baby in a rubbish dump and care for her as they track down her family.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Dress To The Nines – New Year’s Eve Masquerade Ball
item.description: A dressed-up New Year’s Eve celebration in Sheffield with 80s and 90s R&B, soul and old-school classics from DJ Stevie Wonder and DJ Rugged.

item.title: Clown College
item.description: A 6-week workshop series exploring the fundamentals of clowning – not as a set of acrobatic skills, but as a way of relating to yourself, other people and the world around you. Build your confidence through collective experimentation in a DIY space.

item.description: In 1927, Metropolis had its British premiere, unveiling a vision of the future that has echoed through popular culture for a century. One hundred years to the day, Northern Silents marks this anniversary with a special live‑scored screening.

item.description: Classical Weekend returns in 2027. The biennial festival is one big celebration of classical music – in all manner of forms, in all kinds of places.

item.description: To celebrate Tate Britain’s blockbuster Monet and Time exhibition, Exhibition on Screen brings the story of Claude Monet to cinema screens.

item.description: Browse a diverse range of works from 14 talented Sheffield artists. With delicious food and drinks available from Daughters Deli and framing advice from Capstone Framing.
